summary: Learn grain-first warehouse design, star schemas and SCD rules. Review practical design artefacts in this five-day course.
lede: Data warehousing and dimensional modeling turn source events into structures for consistent analysis. For data analysts, reporting specialists and warehouse developers, the training covers defining business grain, designing fact and dimension tables, mapping source-to-target transformations, and handling historical changes with Type 1 and Type 2 slowly changing dimensions. It also includes checks for keys, data quality and source-to-target totals.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who define, build, validate or depend on warehouse structures and need to connect source events to analytical facts and dimensions.
modules: Kimball Bus Matrix and Business Grain
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with business reports and tabular data is useful. No dimensional-modeling experience or programming is required.
